boundary: Reduced public demo data. The 10 visible risks use source-backed text from selected AIRUM risk matrix rows shown in this repository, while the complete AIRUM data core and selection methodology are not published.

riskUniverse.label: AIRUM Part 1
riskUniverse.omittedRiskNote: The complete AIRUM risk universe contains more risks than shown here; this repository intentionally publishes only this 10-risk source-backed subset.

risks.name: AI Ambition-Feasibility Mismatch
risks.description: Pursuing disruptive AI ambitions without the requisite technology maturity, data readiness, or organizational buy-in, leading to project failure.
risks.expectedControlName: AI strategy feasibility and readiness review
risks.expectedControlDescription: Require each material AI ambition, roadmap item, or major use case to document business objective, feasibility assumptions, data/process readiness, capability gaps, funding, accountable owner, and decision gate before investment approval.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Confirm AI ambitions are achievable, resourced, and aligned to realistic organizational readiness before commitments are made.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (Gartner: AI Roadmap; Gartner: AI Strategy; ISO/IEC 42001 (Context of Org); NIST AI RMF: MAP 1.1, MAP 1.2). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.

risks.name: Lack of Clear Accountability
risks.description: Roles for AI development, oversight, and "human-in-the-loop" decision rights are not clearly defined, leading to responsibility gaps.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Assign documented business, technical, risk, data, model, vendor, and control owners for each material AI system, including decision rights and escalation paths.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Make AI ownership, decision accountability, and control responsibility explicit and testable.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (Gartner: AI Organization; MITRE: Org Structure; ISO/IEC 42001 (Roles A.3.2); NIST AI RMF: GOVERN 2.1, GOVERN 2.3). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.

risks.name: Missing AI Inventory
risks.description: Failure to maintain a complete, current inventory of AI systems, models, use cases, automations, and owners prevents risk classification, oversight, monitoring, and compliance.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Maintain a complete and periodically reconciled AI inventory capturing owner, purpose, process, data, vendor, classification, lifecycle stage, and control status for material AI use.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Ensure AI use is visible, owned, classified, and available for risk management and audit scoping.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (Gartner: AI Governance (Inventory); ISO/IEC 5338; ISO/IEC 42001 (Resources A.4.2); NIST AI RMF: MAP 2.1, MANAGE 1.1). risks.name: Sensitive Data Disclosure & Inference
risks.description: Exposure of PII/IP via Model Inversion, Membership Inference, or memorization of sensitive training data.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Apply data minimization, access control, masking, prompt/output safeguards, inference-risk review, logging, and privacy/security testing for AI systems handling sensitive or confidential data.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Prevent unauthorized disclosure, leakage, or inference of sensitive information through AI systems.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (OWASP LLM Top 10: LLM06; OWASP ML Top 10: ML03, ML04; ISO/IEC 42001 (Privacy B.7.2); NIST AI RMF: MEASURE 2.7, MANAGE 2.4). risks.name: Inadequate Verification & Validation
risks.description: Failure to rigorously test AI models for accuracy, robustness, bias, and security prior to deployment, leading to performance failures.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Define and execute independent validation before release, including acceptance criteria, test data, performance, robustness, bias, security, limitations, and approval evidence.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Confirm AI systems meet intended requirements and risk tolerances before operational reliance.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (ISO/IEC 5338 (Verification); ISO/IEC 42001 (Control A.6.2.4); MITRE: Test & Evaluation; NIST AI RMF: MEASURE 1.1, MEASURE 2.6). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.

risks.name: Prompt Injection & Input Manipulation
risks.description: Crafting adversarial inputs to manipulate model behavior, bypass filters, or execute unauthorized actions.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Test and mitigate prompt injection and malicious input scenarios using input validation, instruction hierarchy, retrieval/tool isolation, output constraints, monitoring, and user education.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Reduce the likelihood that hostile inputs override AI instructions, expose data, or trigger unauthorized actions.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (OWASP LLM Top 10: LLM01; OWASP ML Top 10: ML01; Gartner: AI Governance; NIST AI RMF: MANAGE 2.5, MEASURE 2.6). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.

risks.name: Inadequate or Missing AI Governance Framework
risks.description: The organization lacks a formalized AI risk and compliance framework (or the existing one is insufficient) to manage obligations.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Establish and periodically review an AI governance framework covering policy, roles, risk appetite, lifecycle controls, inventory, classification, monitoring, incidents, and reporting.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Provide a coherent management system for governing AI risks across the organization.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (Gartner: AI Governance; MITRE: Governance; ISO/IEC 42001 (Clause 4.4, A.2); NIST AI RMF: GOVERN 1.1, GOVERN 2.1). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.

risks.name: AI Supply Chain & Third-Party Risk
risks.description: Vulnerabilities in the AI supply chain, including compromised third-party models, training data, or ambiguity in vendor contracts.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Assess AI vendors, models, datasets, plugins, APIs, and service providers for security, privacy, resilience, transparency, contractual, and monitoring requirements before and during use.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Control AI-related dependencies and supplier risks across the lifecycle.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (OWASP LLM Top 10: LLM05; OWASP ML Top 10: ML06; ISO/IEC 42001 (Suppliers A.10.3); NIST AI RMF: MANAGE 1.3, MAP 2.3). risks.name: Metadata & Lineage Management Failure
risks.description: Failure to manage technical metadata, lineage, and data/model documentation as operational infrastructure, weakening traceability, reproducibility, explainability, and internal governance over data and model dependencies.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Capture and maintain data origin, transformations, ownership, quality checks, access history, and lineage for datasets used in material AI systems.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Make AI data traceable, explainable, and auditable across collection, preparation, use, and change.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (Gartner: AI Data Guide; ISO/IEC 5338; ISO/IEC 42001 (Provenance A.7.5); NIST AI RMF: MAP 2.3). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.

risks.name: Hallucinations (Confabulation)
risks.description: The model produces factually incorrect results that users accept as truth, compromising decision-making and eroding trust.
risks.expectedControlName: AI output accuracy and grounding control
risks.expectedControlDescription: Require grounding, source citation where feasible, confidence/limitation disclosure, human review for material outputs, and testing of hallucination-prone workflows.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Reduce reliance on fabricated, inaccurate, or unsupported AI outputs.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (Gartner: AI Governance; MITRE: Robust & Reliable; MIT AI Risk Rep: 3.1; NIST AI RMF: MEASURE 2.3). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.
